manuscript: S1-S2 entire-input operator and arbitrary scalar functional
component: S1-S2 entire-input operator and arbitrary scalar functional
hypotheses: Complex coefficient row; entire zero-constant input pairs. No continuity, locality or polynomial ansatz is imposed on H.
boundary: Function.FactorsThrough is equivalent to existence of H on the whole scalar-function space, not merely to an ansatz for the field.

manuscript: H.1 polynomial fiber discriminator and row-sum obstruction
component: H.1 polynomial fiber discriminator and row-sum obstruction
hypotheses: All four scales positive, with repeated nodes allowed. No upper bound on scales. The first row coordinate is nonzero only after retaining the nonzero-row premise.
boundary: Three exact algebraic fiber comparisons replace differentiation of xy. No distinct-node interpolation hypothesis is added.

manuscript: H.1 ordered scale recovery, exact row classification and zero field
component: H.1 ordered scale recovery, exact row classification and zero field
hypotheses: Positive scales; nonzero row for the manuscript classification. The generalized version retains the zero-row exception. Sufficiency is pointwise for arbitrary functions.
boundary: Ordered q=a and r=b are necessary. Swapped unequal rows may give canonical U=V but do not give a nonzero autonomous operator row.

manuscript: H.1 no invertible constant linear decoupling
component: H.1 no invertible constant linear decoupling
hypotheses: Any complex 2x2 matrix whose two rows are autonomous, including zero rows, has zero determinant. Invertibility is IsUnit of the actual matrix.
boundary: This is a constant linear operator obstruction. Nonlinear transformations or elimination along a particular solution are not excluded.

manuscript: S1-S3 local analytic germs and arbitrary germ functional
component: S1-S3 local analytic germs and arbitrary germ functional
hypotheses: Inputs analytic at zero and vanishing there; equality in Filter.Germ at the neighborhood filter. Positive scales for equivalence/classification, not for the entire identity-principle implication.
boundary: Scalar functionals on germs are arbitrary. The field respects representative germs, and whole-plane equality for entire tests follows from local equality by the pinned identity principle.
